Skip to main content
Ukrainian drones attack Russia’s Samara region, reportedly striking Europe’s largest oil storage facility
November 2, 2026, 8:16 am
Source: Astra
Ukrainian drones struck Russia’s Samara region overnight on November 2. Regional authorities had not officially commented on the strikes by the time of publication, but Samara’s airport suspended operations for two hours because of the drone threat.
Ukrainian monitoring channels and Astra, an independent Telegram channel, cited photos and videos from eyewitnesses in reporting that the drones, according to preliminary reports, struck the Samara Linear Production and Dispatch Station (LPDS) near the settlement of Prosvet.
The Samara LPDS is the largest tank farm in Europe, part of a network operated by Transneft. Four pipelines carrying oil from Western Siberia, Tatarstan, the Orenburg region, and Kazakhstan connect to the station.
Ukrainian military drones struck the Samara LPDS several times in October, causing fires and damaging storage tanks.

Russia said its emergency warnings app came under a "massive cyberattack" on Monday, hours after Ukraine reported a hack in an apparent exchange of blows between the foes, as their longest truce came to an end.
Moscow's emergencies ministry said hackers posted "false information" on the app, which is designed to warn the public of incoming drone attacks and other threats.
Hours earlier, Ukraine said it suspected its air raid alert system had been compromised, after baseless alerts of a radiation threat appeared on the app.
The cyber attacks came as the longest truce of the war, limited to Ukraine's eastern Kherson region, ended on Sunday after Russia refused the offer of an extension, according to Kyiv. 
Moscow did not immediately say who was behind the attack on its app, while Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications SPRAVDI blamed the hack it suffered on Russia.

Russia’s state statistics agency Rosstat said Sunday that its websites had been hit by a coordinated cyberattack, while hackers claimed to have stolen 23 terabytes of data, including information on Russian losses in the war in Ukraine.
Messages from the Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow hacking groups appeared on the agency’s main website and regional portals, Rosstat told the RBC news website. Among them was a message in Belarusian reading: “No one will escape accountability.”
Both groups are designated as extremist and banned in Russia.
Rosstat said the attacks took place between Oct. 29 and Nov. 1 and were carefully planned, targeting several areas simultaneously and involving specialists with different expertise operating from a wide range of locations.

Russia’s Justice Ministry has added the Dialogue with Russian Democratic Forces at the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) to its list of “undesirable” organizations, a move that renders affiliation with the anti-war group illegal.
The delegation of Russian exiles was set up in January after years of lobbying efforts by leading opposition figures like former businessman Mikhail Khodorkovsky.

Skip to main content
Pentagon urges Baltic NATO allies to tone down rhetoric about Russia, citing remarks likening Putin to a ‘rat in a corner’
October 30, 2026, 8:49 am
Source: Reuters
Pentagon officials urged several NATO member countries to tone down their rhetoric about the Russian threat during bilateral meetings, according to Reuters sources.
The requests went to Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia, among others, the agency’s sources said. It is unclear whether other countries received similar requests.
Elbridge Colby, head of the Pentagon’s policy directorate, was one of the officials who conveyed the requests. He cited public statements by Europeans describing Russia as “cornered like a rat” as an example of inappropriate rhetoric.
It is unclear which statement he meant, but in late September, Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal called Putin a “rat in a corner” and suggested that Russia is resorting to sabotage in Europe because it is increasingly bogged down in the war with Ukraine, Reuters said.

titulekPuvodni: Four jet-powered drones attacked Dnipropetrovsk Oblast: three downed, one hit Dnipro station – Air Force
shrnuti: Ukraine's air defence shot down three of four jet-powered Russian drones over Dnipropetrovsk Oblast; the fourth hit a railway station in Dnipro, killing 13 and injuring 13.

vyrez.text:
Ukraine's Air Force: one of four jet-powered drones hit Dnipro station platform | Ukrainska Pravda
Fatalities resulting from the Russian strike on the railway station in Dnipro. Photo: State Emergency Service
Ukraine's Air Force has reported that air defence shot down three of the four jet-powered drones used by Russian forces to attack Dnipropetrovsk Oblast on the afternoon of 29 October. One drone struck Dnipro, killing 13 people.
Source: Ukraine's Air Force on Telegram
Details: The Russians attacked the region at around 11:00.
Advertisement:





"The enemy directed four jet-powered attack drones at Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. Three were destroyed by air defence. Unfortunately, one drone struck the railway station platform in Dnipro," the Air Force reported.
As of 13:00, the number of people injured has risen to 13.
Background: On 29 October, Russian forces attacked a railway station in Dnipro with a jet-powered drone. The strike hit the platform where train No. 866 (Dnipro-Zaporizhzhia) was standing. Thirteen people are known to have been killed and at least 10 injured.

Ruská protivzdušná obrana v noci na čtvrtek nad mnoha částmi Ruska zničila 1214 ukrajinských bezpilotních letounů, uvedlo podle agentury TASS ministerstvo obrany v Moskvě. Noční útok na Moskvu byl podle agentury jedním z nejrozsáhlejších od začátku letošního roku. Starosta metropole Sergej Sobjanin na platformě Max napsal, že od středy 20:30 do dnešních 07:00 mířilo k moskevskému regionu 613 dronů. Většinu z nich se podle něj podařilo zničit ve větší vzdálenosti od hlavního města, dalších 231 při přiblížení k Moskvě.

The deployment of 500 paratroopers to Milan to quell violent protests by teenagers marks a surprising shift in the use of soldiers to maintain public order. The sight of Lince tactical vehicles beneath the Gothic spires of Milan’s Duomo looked more like a government PR stunt than a solution to the unrest that had erupted in the city centre. And a look back at history seems to bear this out: in the past, bringing in the army has always marked dramatic moments in the country’s history.
The secret mission of 1961
The first deployment remains the least known, and was indeed shrouded in secrecy. Schutz von Kritischer Infrastruktur
Bund beschließt mehr Prüfungen auf Sabotagerisiko
Stand: 28.10.2026 • 15:48 Uhr
Die Bedrohung für die Kritische Infrastruktur in Deutschland - etwa durch Sabotage oder Spionage - ist gestiegen. Daher will der Bund künftig Beschäftigte in noch mehr Betrieben auf mögliche Sicherheitsrisiken überprüfen.
Das Bundeskabinett hat eine Ausweitung der Sicherheitsüberprüfung von Beschäftigten in wichtigen Betrieben der Kritischen Infrastruktur beschlossen. Das soll das Risiko von Sabotageaktionen mit extremistischem Hintergrund oder im Auftrag eines ausländischen Geheimdienstes reduzieren.
Die Verordnung soll Einrichtungen wie etwa die Bahn oder Wasserwerke vor gefährlichen Eingriffen sogenannter Innentäter, also Menschen mit Zugang zu wichtigen Anlagen, schützen. Dafür wird neu bestimmt, welche Behörden und Unternehmensteile sicherheitsempfindlich sind.

titulek: Leaders of Finland and Norway talk to Putin
titulekPuvodni: Leaders of Finland and Norway talk to Putin
shrnuti: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian PM Jonas Gahr Støre initiated the call to discuss efforts to end the Ukraine war.

vyrez.text:
Leaders of Finland and Norway talk to Putin – POLITICO
Skip to main content
Advertisement
Finland’s President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a joint call with Russian leader Vladimir Putin on Tuesday as part of international efforts to secure an end to the war in Ukraine.
“The discussion was frank and substantive,” said Stubb said in a statement after the call. “We are neighboring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions.”
The two leaders — who are firm allies of Ukraine — were not speaking as official representatives of Europe as a whole. The call was held in consultation with Ukraine.
Støre said the European leaders stressed the importance of de-escalation in the call with Putin. “The war comes with enormous human and material costs. The suffering and destruction will impact generations,” he added.
Their conversation comes at a highly sensitive moment as U.S. President Donald Trump pushes for a peace deal. Talks between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine are planned to take place in Abu Dhabi next month.

US President Donald Trump has launched a fresh verbal attack on Norway, branding the wealthy Nordic nation a “shithouse country”.

Speaking at a rally in Port Huron, Michigan, on Sunday, Trump tied his remarks to his repeated frustration over being denied the Nobel Peace Prize.
Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway "because I didn't get the Nobel Prize." "So I don't want anybody from Norway," he said.
Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump's comments on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent.
